issues.description: The problem statement and template expect an interface named 'Rideable' (see UML and example usage in Main), but the solution repository defines an interface named 'Mountable' (Mountable.java) and leaves Rideable.java empty. Classes in the solution (Pig, Seal) implement Mountable instead of Rideable. This name/type mismatch between the expected interface and the solution will confuse students and break code that references Rideable (e.g., the template's Main and the UML), preventing them from compiling or implementing the intended design.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Either rename 'Mountable' to 'Rideable' in the solution and have Pig and Seal implement Rideable, and remove or populate Rideable.java accordingly; or update the problem statement and template to use 'Mountable' instead of 'Rideable'. Ensure only one interface file defines messageOnRide() and that its name matches the UML and template usage.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to an interface named 'Rideable' (with method messageOnRide()), but the solution implementation introduces an interface named 'Mountable' and leaves Rideable.java empty. Pig and Seal implement 'Mountable' in the solution, while the exercise text and template Main expect 'Rideable'. This inconsistency breaks the direct mapping students must make from the problem description to the provided/expected code and can cause confusion about which interface to implement or use.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across artifacts. Either (A) rename Mountable.java to Rideable.java (and update Pig.java and Seal.java to implement Rideable) and ensure Rideable.java declares String messageOnRide(); or (B) update the problem statement and template to refer to 'Mountable' instead of 'Rideable'. Prefer option A to match the exercise text and template.
